summary: Local macOS test-only retained double-double fine factor, projection and final coordinate correction, compared with and without bounded fine-coordinate rounding selection. Binary-scaled Gram/LDL recovers independent nearly parallel analytic columns across row orders, scales and signs, and a one-third correction confirms that premature rounding can change a known final result. From identical 128-element actual modal polisher seeds, the automatic half partition preserves sampled unit/large-coordinate passing shapes with independent physical reassembly and constructed complete result JSON readback; fine rounding selection improves those residuals only slightly. The one-anchor partition rejects all three sampled scales, and every tiny-coordinate candidate family remains explicitly rejected near 1.740427e-8. Separate work/payload plans, one 80-check counter, cached factor reuse, fresh final certificates and cancellation/replay are tested. This proves scoped diagnosis and control, not new runtime admission, arbitrary-precision/interval guarantees, general representability, multimode qualification, measured performance or live Agent/installed/remote execution.
